title: Zenith Coordinator (ZC): A Traceable State-Machine Coordination Layer for Interbank Payments
description:
Zenith Coordinator (ZC) is a reference implementation of a coordination layer that treats interbank payments as a fixed sequence of state transitions — Received → Decision → Execution Confirmation → Settled — and records every transition in an append-only, hash-chained FinalityLog. It runs end-to-end on TypeScript and Cloudflare Workers.

ZC does not replace any participant's core banking or account-management systems. Instead, it coordinates what happens "between" those systems, so that every party involved in a transaction — payer, payee, or supervising authority — can later be given the same explanation, referencing the same transaction ID, the same timestamps, and the same reason codes.

Design principles include: a single source of truth (the FinalityLog, from which derived views can always be rebuilt); strict separation between Decision and Execution; an irreversibility boundary at payee execution confirmation, with any later remedy handled as a separate reversal transaction; a prohibition on unexplainable states, with unresolved or inconsistent states always converging to a CASE; contractually fixed semantics for synchronous responses; no after-the-fact evidence; lanes defined by finality point and evidentiary contract rather than UX; sending-bank overdraft headroom managed as explicit state with no silent breach; crisis handling modeled as institutionalized state transitions rather than exceptions; and single-source-of-truth guarantees backed by a distributed consensus log that degrades to read-only under uncertainty.

The project also treats traditional payment rails (RTGS, DNS netting, domestic retail clearing, ISO 20022, FATF Recommendation 16) and newer primitives (hash-time-locked contracts, atomic multi-leg settlement) as peer lanes on a single shared state machine, rather than as separate systems bridged together.

This is an independent, personal project. It uses no confidential material of any kind and does not depict, represent, or reference any real organization, institution, system, or operational practice.
